subject: business-studies
title: Break-Even: Where Revenue Catches Total Cost

segments.say: Axes first, then the flat fixed-cost line. Rent and insurance cost $2,000 however much the business makes, so the fixed-cost line stays flat at $2,000 at every output. Point at the flat line on your student notes diagram before any other line is drawn.
questions: What stays at $2,000 at every output, and why?
What do the two axes measure on a break-even chart?

segments.say: Total cost starts at fixed costs, then rises. At zero output total cost is already $2,000, and each extra unit adds $10 of variable cost. Now try the total-cost questions on your worksheet.
questions: Where does the total-cost line start, and why not at zero?
How much does total cost rise for each extra unit made?

segments.say: Revenue rises faster, but still in loss. Total revenue starts at zero and rises by $20 for each unit sold, faster than total cost rises, but below 200 units total cost is still above revenue. Check the loss zone against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Which line rises faster, revenue or total cost, and by how much per unit?
Why is there still a loss even though revenue is catching up?

segments.say: Break-even, then the profit zone opens. At 200 units revenue and total cost both equal $4,000, and above 200 units revenue is above total cost so profit opens. Keep the flat, intercept, faster-revenue, crossing order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: How do you prove 200 units is the break-even output?
What are the four stages of building the break-even chart, in order?
segments.watchFor: Fixed costs rise as output rises, so total cost starts at zero like revenue. Listen for students who start total cost at zero or let fixed costs climb with output. Send them back to scene 2 and the $2,000 intercept: Fixed costs stay flat at $2,000 at every output, so total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept and rises only by the $10 variable cost per unit; total revenue starts at zero and rises faster at the $20 selling price, so the two lines cross once, at the break-even output of 200 units.
